learning_outcomes.text: Applies the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.
Applies experimental techniques to mechanical systems.

Correctly applies the principles of calculation for single-degree-of-freedom vibratory systems. Knows the different techniques for measuring vibrations, noise, and unbalances in machines and can interpret the measurements obtained with these devices.

Intervenes effectively and transmits relevant information, appropriate to the situation. Plans communication: generates ideas, searches for information, selects and orders information, creates outlines, determines the type of audience, communication objectives,... Drafts documents with the appropriate format, content, structure, linguistic correctness, register, and illustrates concepts correctly using conventions: formats, titles, footnotes, legends,... Their presentations are properly prepared, using strategies to present and carry out their oral presentations (audiovisual aids, gaze, voice, gesture, time control,...).

Participates actively and shares information, knowledge, and experiences. Contributes individually within the planned time and with available resources. Accepts and complies with group norms. Actively collaborates in team work planning, task distribution, and required deadlines.

Collects significant information needed to solve problems based on objective criteria. Follows a logical method to identify the causes of a problem. Presents different alternative solution options for the same problem and evaluates their possible risks and advantages. Develops a strategy to solve the problem. Obtains necessary support from others to ensure the success of their decisions. Has the ability to lead the decision-making process participatively. Systematically questions new ways of doing things, seeks new procedures, and experiments with new procedures. Analyzes risks and benefits of innovation.

syllabus_topics: Schematization and simulation of real mechanisms. Application of the theoretical concepts of Kinematics of mechanisms from Mechanics and Theory of Mechanisms I and II.
Moment of inertia. Dynamic reduction of single-degree-of-freedom mechanisms. Balancing of dynamic rotors. Static balancing of a bicycle.
Kinematic design of plate cam mechanisms with translating follower. How does a car's gearbox work?
teaching_methods: Introductory activities: Course presentation. How it is organized and evaluated.
Master class: Explanation of theory and objectives of the practical work to be done. An online test will be conducted at the end of each master class to assess acquired knowledge.

Laboratory practices: Practical work carried out in laboratory 07. The material will be specified in the practice guide. All documentation can be found on the course Moodle. A complete practice report will be submitted to the instructor at the end of the practice.
assessment_rules: To qualify for continuous assessment, the minimum score for the test exam must be 4.0 or higher, and the minimum score for the oral exam must be 4.0 or higher. To pass the course, students must have attended ALL practical sessions in person; only one justified absence is permitted according to regulations. In case of a justified absence, the student will complete a substitute assignment for that practical session, with a maximum possible grade of 5.0. This work must be requested from the responsible instructor within one week after the theoretical date of the practical session, and the student has one week to submit it. If repeating the course, if the overall grade for practical guides does not exceed 6.0, the student must repeat ALL practical sessions. This course has a SINGLE assessment call.
